q: Hazzard describes increasing difficulty focusing on near targets beginning around age 45. Which mechanism accounts for this age-related loss of accommodation?
o: Reduced pupil size and reduced light transmission impair near accommodation.
Reduced lens flexibility and reduced ciliary muscle tone impair near accommodation.
Macular degeneration and loss of central retinal fixation impair near accommodation.
Peripheral visual-field loss and reduced obstacle detection impair near accommodation.
explanation:
**Accommodation** depends on the flexible crystalline lens and the ciliary muscle. Age-related loss of lens flexibility and ciliary muscle tone explains the increasing difficulty with near focus described in the table (p. 471). "Crystalline lenses lose flexibility" (p. 471).

**A. Reduced pupil size and reduced light transmission impair near accommodation.** Wrong, reduced pupil size and light transmission are assigned to loss of low-contrast acuity, not the accommodative mechanism (p. 471).
**B. Reduced lens flexibility and reduced ciliary muscle tone impair near accommodation.** Correct, this matches the structural changes listed under decreased accommodation (p. 471).
**C. Macular degeneration and loss of central retinal fixation impair near accommodation.** Wrong, macular disease is not the lens-and-ciliary-muscle mechanism identified for age-related loss of accommodation (p. 471).
**D. Peripheral visual-field loss and reduced obstacle detection impair near accommodation.** Wrong, peripheral-field loss does not describe the lens and ciliary changes responsible for the near-focusing deficit (p. 471).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 471.

q: רופא מדווח למרב״ד על מצב רפואי קבוע העלול לסכן נהיגה. איזה תיאור של משמעות הדיווח נכון לפי החוזר?
o: הדיווח קובע פסילה מיידית של הרישיון ללא הערכה נוספת
הדיווח מפנה לבדיקה לצורך המלצה על הגבלות נהיגה
הדיווח מעביר לרופא המטפל סמכות להנפיק רישיון מוגבל
הדיווח מחייב חזרה לנהיגה רגילה אם הראייה נמצאה תקינה
explanation:
**בדיקת המרב״ד** נועדה להעריך כשירות ולהמליץ לרשות הרישוי על המשך נהיגה, לרבות הגבלות ואביזרים. עצם ההודעה אינו שקול לפסילה מיידית, ובינתיים הרופא ממליץ להפסיק נהיגה עד לבדיקה (עמ׳ 3).
"בסמכות המרב"ד להמליץ לרשות הרישוי על המשך נהיגה, תוך הגבלות שונות, או שימוש באביזרים שמטרתם לאפשר בטיחות בנהיגה." (עמ׳ 3).

**א. הדיווח קובע פסילה מיידית של הרישיון ללא הערכה נוספת.** שגויה, החוזר מבהיר במפורש שהודעת הרופא אינה פסילת רישיון מיידית (עמ׳ 3, סעיף 7.4).
**ב. הדיווח מפנה לבדיקה לצורך המלצה על הגבלות נהיגה.** נכונה, המרב״ד רשאי להמליץ לרשות הרישוי על הגבלות או אביזרים המאפשרים נהיגה בטוחה (עמ׳ 3, סעיף 7.5).
**ג. הדיווח מעביר לרופא המטפל סמכות להנפיק רישיון מוגבל.** שגויה, הסמכות המתוארת היא המלצת המרב״ד לרשות הרישוי, ולא הנפקת רישיון בידי הרופא המטפל (עמ׳ 3, סעיף 7.5).
**ד. הדיווח מחייב חזרה לנהיגה רגילה אם הראייה נמצאה תקינה.** שגויה, החלטה על המשך נהיגה דורשת הערכת המרב״ד בהקשר למצב הרפואי, ולא חזרה אוטומטית על סמך ראייה תקינה (עמ׳ 3, סעיפים 7.1 ו-7.5).

מקור: 10Redefiningtheobligation.pdf עמ׳ 3.

q: During counseling about radiation after NSCLC resection, what does Hazzard report from LungART for patients upstaged to stage IIIA because of N2 nodal involvement?
o: Lower cardiopulmonary toxicity with an overall-survival advantage
Higher cardiopulmonary toxicity without a demonstrated survival advantage
Lower cardiopulmonary toxicity without a demonstrated survival advantage
Higher cardiopulmonary toxicity with an overall-survival advantage
explanation:
**Postoperative radiation in LungART** is described as increasing cardiopulmonary toxicity without demonstrating the stated survival benefit in this N2 population. The chapter reports "higher cardiopulmonary toxicity" with "no 3-year disease-free survival and overall survival advantage" (p. 1426). These are the trial findings as presented in the cited edition.

**A. Lower cardiopulmonary toxicity with an overall-survival advantage.** Wrong, the source reports increased toxicity and no demonstrated overall-survival advantage, so both parts conflict with the reported findings (p. 1426).
**B. Higher cardiopulmonary toxicity without a demonstrated survival advantage.** Correct, this combines the increased cardiopulmonary toxicity with the absence of demonstrated disease-free or overall-survival benefit (p. 1426).
**C. Lower cardiopulmonary toxicity without a demonstrated survival advantage.** Wrong, the lack of demonstrated survival benefit is consistent, but cardiopulmonary toxicity increased rather than decreased (p. 1426).
**D. Higher cardiopulmonary toxicity with an overall-survival advantage.** Wrong, the toxicity direction is consistent, but the source does not report an overall-survival advantage (p. 1426).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1426.

q: בן 80 עם סרטן לבלב גרורתי שוקל ERCP להקלה על חסימה. הוא מסוגל להחליט ואומר שברצונו לבלות זמן עם נכדיו; אשתו מדגישה הימנעות מאשפוז. לפני המלצה משותפת, איזה צעד שומר על בחירה מדעת של המטופל?
o: להעמיד את שיעור ההצלחה הטכנית כמדד המכריע בהחלטה
לברר את העדפותיו ולהסביר תועלת, סיכונים וחלופות
להעמיד את העדפת אשתו לזמן בבית כמדד המכריע בהחלטה
להעמיד את תוספת ההישרדות המשוערת כמדד המכריע בהחלטה
explanation:
**בחירה מדעת** מחייבת למסור מידע באופן המאפשר למטופל להבין ולבחור מרצונו. מכאן, כיישום של העיקרון, יש לברר עמו מה חשוב לו ואיך הוא שוקל זמן, סבל ואשפוז, במקום לייחס לו את העדפת בן המשפחה או לקבוע מדד יחיד (סעיף 13, עמ׳ 8).
"באופן שיאפשר למטופל מידה מרבית של הבנת המידע לשם קבלת החלטה בדרך של בחירה מרצון ואי תלות." (עמ׳ 8).

**א. להעמיד את שיעור ההצלחה הטכנית כמדד המכריע בהחלטה.** שגויה, הצלחה טכנית אינה כוללת את מלוא התועלת, הסיכונים והחלופות שהמטופל צריך לשקול (סעיף 13, עמ׳ 8).
**ב. לברר את העדפותיו ולהסביר תועלת, סיכונים וחלופות.** נכונה, הסבר האפשרויות ובירור העדפותיו מאפשרים לו לקבל החלטה מרצונו; זהו יישום של עקרון ההסכמה מדעת (סעיף 13, עמ׳ 8).
**ג. להעמיד את העדפת אשתו לזמן בבית כמדד המכריע בהחלטה.** שגויה, העדפת האישה אינה בחירתו של מטופל המסוגל להחליט; יש לברר את רצונו שלו (סעיף 13, עמ׳ 8).
**ד. להעמיד את תוספת ההישרדות המשוערת כמדד המכריע בהחלטה.** שגויה, הישרדות היא מידע רלוונטי, אך אינה מחליפה דיון בסיכונים ובחלופות ובחירה מרצון (סעיף 13, עמ׳ 8).

מקור: חוק זכויות החולה, תשנ_ו-1996.pdf עמ׳ 8.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: An 81-year-old man with advanced COPD has refractory dyspnea despite optimal treatment of the underlying disease. An opioid is being considered for palliation. Which potential benefit and cognitive risk are described by Hazzard?
o: Relief of dyspnea with a risk of reduced mental functioning
Relief of dyspnea with an expected improvement in mental functioning
Worsening dyspnea with a risk of reduced mental functioning
Worsening dyspnea with an expected improvement in mental functioning
explanation:
**Opioids for refractory dyspnea** may provide benefit, although study findings are not consistent. In older adults they are associated with decreased mental functioning, a tradeoff that some patients find unacceptable despite potential breathing relief (p. 1074).
"In patients with refractory dyspnea, opioids may be beneficial." (p. 1074).

**A. Relief of dyspnea with a risk of reduced mental functioning.** Correct, this preserves both the potential respiratory benefit and the described cognitive risk (p. 1074).
**B. Relief of dyspnea with an expected improvement in mental functioning.** Wrong, the source describes decreased mental functioning as a risk, not cognitive improvement as the expected benefit (p. 1074).
**C. Worsening dyspnea with a risk of reduced mental functioning.** Wrong, the cited therapeutic rationale is potential dyspnea relief, not worsening of dyspnea, alongside the cognitive risk (p. 1074).
**D. Worsening dyspnea with an expected improvement in mental functioning.** Wrong, both components conflict with the source's described potential relief and risk of reduced mental functioning (p. 1074).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1074.
ref: Hazzard Ch 69 — MANAGEMENT OF COMMON NONPAIN SYMPTOMS

q: A patient receiving antiresorptive treatment underwent a tooth extraction. An area of exposed, necrotic jaw bone has now failed to heal for ten weeks. Which complication matches this finding?
o: An atypical insufficiency fracture of the femur during antiresorptive treatment
Reduced bone density measured during the course of antiresorptive treatment
Osteonecrosis of the jaw associated with antiresorptive treatment
Joint pain without bone damage following the use of antiresorptive treatment
explanation:
**Osteonecrosis of the jaw** is associated with antiresorptive treatment, and invasive dental procedures may increase its risk (p. 777). Hazzard defines it as "the presence of exposed and necrotic bone in the maxillofacial region that does not heal within 8 weeks." (p. 777). The ten-week lesion described in the stem fits that definition.

**A. An atypical insufficiency fracture of the femur during antiresorptive treatment.** Wrong, atypical femoral fractures are located in the subtrochanteric region or femoral shaft, not the maxillofacial site described here (p. 777).
**B. Reduced bone density measured during the course of antiresorptive treatment.** Wrong, a density measurement does not characterize the exposed, necrotic, nonhealing lesion; the source defines this clinical finding as osteonecrosis of the jaw (p. 777).
**C. Osteonecrosis of the jaw associated with antiresorptive treatment.** Correct, the anatomical site, exposed necrotic bone, and failure to heal beyond eight weeks match the definition (p. 777).
**D. Joint pain without bone damage following the use of antiresorptive treatment.** Wrong, the stem documents necrotic bone; a description without bone damage misses the defining lesion (p. 777).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 777.

q: For a basal cell carcinoma located in a low-risk area, which combination of life expectancy and additional lesion risk does Hazzard describe for discussing active surveillance?
o: Prolonged life expectancy and a lesion with additional risk factors
Limited life expectancy and a lesion without additional risk factors
Limited life expectancy and a lesion with additional risk factors
Prolonged life expectancy and a lesion without additional risk factors
explanation:
**Active surveillance for selected BCCs** is discussed for limited life expectancy and low-risk lesions. BCCs are generally indolent and slow-growing, so monitoring can avoid unnecessary treatment while watching for growth or symptoms; it is not described as the standard of care (p. 1463). "some providers also consider active surveillance appropriate when lesions are in low-risk areas without other risk factors." (p. 1463).

**A. Prolonged life expectancy and a lesion with additional risk factors.** Wrong, neither the limited life expectancy nor the low-risk lesion conditions of the described surveillance scenario are present (p. 1463).
**B. Limited life expectancy and a lesion without additional risk factors.** Correct, it matches both conditions in the source discussion of a possible surveillance option (p. 1463).
**C. Limited life expectancy and a lesion with additional risk factors.** Wrong, limited life expectancy fits, but the presence of additional lesion risk factors does not match the low-risk scenario described (p. 1463).
**D. Prolonged life expectancy and a lesion without additional risk factors.** Wrong, low lesion risk fits, but the source discussion also specifies limited life expectancy; it does not establish this long-life-expectancy scenario (p. 1463).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1463.

q: A 72-year-old man with obesity (BMI 38), fatigue, reduced libido, and a total testosterone level of 8.5 nmol/L sleeps poorly and snores. Which approach is supported before considering testosterone treatment?
o: Begin testosterone replacement and postpone evaluation of the suspected sleep disorder
Arrange sleep testing and encourage weight reduction while evaluating the testosterone deficiency
Treat the low testosterone as irreversible and prioritize replacement over evaluating underlying causes
Use DHEA replacement and postpone evaluation of the suspected sleep disorder
explanation:
**Low testosterone** requires etiologic assessment, including potentially reversible functional causes (p. 1534). Snoring and obesity raise concern for sleep-disordered breathing, for which "Patients suspected of having SDB should be referred for sleep testing." (pp. 646–647). Weight management addresses a relevant background factor, and untreated obstructive sleep apnea is a reason for caution with testosterone (p. 1534; application).

**A. Begin testosterone replacement and postpone evaluation of the suspected sleep disorder.** Wrong, this postpones evaluation of suspected sleep-disordered breathing despite the testing recommendation and the caution concerning untreated obstructive sleep apnea (pp. 647, 1534).
**B. Arrange sleep testing and encourage weight reduction while evaluating the testosterone deficiency.** Correct, sleep testing addresses the suspected breathing disorder while weight management and etiologic assessment address potentially reversible contributors before replacement decisions (pp. 646–647, 1534).
**C. Treat the low testosterone as irreversible and prioritize replacement over evaluating underlying causes.** Wrong, functional hypogonadism can be reversible with treatment of its underlying cause, so an irreversible deficit cannot be assumed from the stated level (p. 1534).
**D. Use DHEA replacement and postpone evaluation of the suspected sleep disorder.** Wrong, substituting another hormone does not meet the recommendation to investigate suspected sleep-disordered breathing (p. 647; application).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 646, 647, 1534.
ref: Hazzard Ch 37 — SEXUALITY , SEXUAL FUNCTION, AND THE AGING MAN
chapterTitle: SEXUALITY , SEXUAL FUNCTION, AND THE AGING MAN

q: בן 80, ברקע סרטן ראות מסוג Small-Cell Lung Carcinoma (SCLC). מספר חודשים סובל מחולשה פרוקסימלית של הידיים והרגליים, קושי להרים ידיים מעל הראש ולעמוד מישיבה, והיפו-רפלקסיה. מה יחזק את האבחנה המשוערת?
o: בבדיקת דם נוגדנים נגד רצפטורי אצטילכולין
חזר לאחרונה מטיול למזרח הרחוק עם אכילה בשווקים
Exophthalmos ו- TSH נמוך
למטופל יש אורטוסטטיזם ופה יבש
explanation:
Proximal weakness, reduced reflexes and small-cell lung cancer suggest **Lambert–Eaton myasthenic syndrome**. Hazzard describes an antibody-mediated defect in acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction and its association with this cancer (p. 1626). Autonomic symptoms reinforce this clinical pattern (Ivanovski and Miralles, Abstract/Clinical manifestations).
"Dry mouth is the most commonly reported symptom" (Ivanovski and Miralles, Clinical manifestations).

**A. Anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies in blood.** Wrong, these support evaluation for myasthenia gravis rather than identifying the antibodies characteristic of the suspected paraneoplastic syndrome. This distinguishes the diagnoses without asserting that overlap is impossible (Rousseff, section 3.1; Hazzard p. 1626).
**B. Recent travel to the Far East with market-food consumption.** Wrong, food exposure may suggest botulism, but travel and market eating alone do not establish it. Botulism evolves over hours to days, unlike the months-long weakness in the stem; this is an inference from the clinical course (Rao et al., Signs and Symptoms).
**C. Exophthalmos and low TSH.** Wrong, these prompt evaluation for Graves disease and hyperthyroidism, rather than specifically supporting the cancer-associated acetylcholine-release disorder. Thyroid hormone levels are needed to interpret low TSH (Hazzard pp. 1549–1550, 1626).
**D. Orthostatic symptoms and dry mouth.** Correct, both are autonomic manifestations described in Lambert–Eaton syndrome. With proximal weakness and reduced reflexes they strengthen suspicion, followed by serological or electrophysiological confirmation (Ivanovski and Miralles, Abstract/Clinical manifestations/Diagnosis).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1549–1550, 1626; Ivanovski T, Miralles F. Lambert-Eaton Myasthenic syndrome: early diagnosis is key. Degener Neurol Neuromuscul Dis. 2019;9:27–37. doi:10.2147/DNND.S192588; Rousseff RT. Diagnosis of Myasthenia Gravis. J Clin Med. 2021;10:1736. doi:10.3390/jcm10081736; Rao AK et al. Clinical Guidelines for Diagnosis and Treatment of Botulism, 2021. MMWR Recomm Rep. 2021;70(2):1–30. doi:10.15585/mmwr.rr7002a1. All three cited external sources were checked.
